narrative:
The model estimates a 60% chance that you will leave your current role, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your work history.

Most influential was the fact that you have spent over 11 years in your current organization. While long tenure often signals loyalty, in this case the model sees it as a strong indicator that you may be ready for a change, pushing the prediction noticeably toward leaving. 

The second strongest factor is that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities available increases the likelihood of departure, pulling the prediction further in the leaving direction.

Your overall career experience of more than 11 years across all roles also contributed, though to a lesser extent. Extensive experience tends to correlate with higher mobility in the dataset, adding a modest push toward leaving.

Taken together, these elements outweighed positive signals such as your satisfaction with rewards, useful training, and feeling you received deserved promotions in the past.

The organization should consider discussing your long-term aspirations and whether additional challenges or growth opportunities could be created internally. For you, it may be worth reflecting on whether the external offers align better with your goals or if there are changes that could make staying more fulfilling. Addressing these points openly could help retain valuable talent like yourself.
